assessment.summary: JAK2 is one of the most extensively validated and drugged kinase targets in human medicine, with 171 PDB structures (best resolution 1.3Å), over 19,000 ChEMBL IC50 entries, and 12 approved drugs including ruxolitinib, baricitinib, and fedratinib. The target has exceptional structural, chemical, and literature support across multiple disease indications including myeloproliferative neoplasms, inflammatory diseases, and cancer. Druggability is unambiguously high by every available metric.
evidence_gaps: Selectivity over closely related JAK family members (JAK1, JAK3, TYK2) remains a challenge for next-generation inhibitors, and isoform-selective structural data may be incomplete for some binding modes
Allosteric binding sites beyond the ATP-competitive pocket are less well characterised structurally
Resistance mechanisms (e.g., JAK2 V617F secondary mutations under drug pressure) are not fully mapped in structural terms
Long-term safety and efficacy data for newer approved agents (e.g., pacritinib, momelotinib) are still accumulating
PROTAC/degrader and covalent inhibitor chemical space is relatively underexplored compared to classical ATP-competitive inhibitors
